craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of forced drawing; vyabhicāri utsāha at sun sapped, difference thinned. Sanskrit-first: mārtāṇḍa normalization recorded per UNC (kept); ākarṣa (DRAW-HARD — kept; triple imperative kept triple). Rows: 9 (draw-hard/thin/free — three verbs pull together), 1 (‘world-fear’ closes — freed-FROM named last). Close: ‘free me from world-fear’. Rupture: em-dash (step described, then she named — narrow step, then sun-sapper). Rejected: triple→single imperative — killed: three verbs pull; ‘sip’ for saps — killed: śoṣaṇa saps entire (totality kept). Read aloud: WHERE do-ing-MIND-mea-sures FAIL, ON the-NARR-ow-STEP … SHE who-SAPS the-STA-tioned-SUN en-TIRE: DRAW-hard, THIN my-DIFF-er-ence, FREE-me FROM-world-FEAR.

lines: Where doing-mind-measures fail, on the narrow step — spreading wide, then drawing in by its own gleams —
she who saps the stationed sun entire: draw hard, thin my difference, free me from world-fear.
